CHIEF COMPLAINT
Evaluation of kidneys for potential congenital anomalies related to Smith-Magenis syndrome.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Katherine is a 22-month-old female born at 34 weeks and 3 days gestation as part of a twin pregnancy. Birth weight was 4 pounds 8 ounces. She was diagnosed with Smith-Magenis syndrome by neurology after presenting with developmental delay, including not sitting by herself by one year of age. She was not walking independently but is now crawling and attempting to take steps. She has a history of feeding difficulties with apnea during feeding and temperature regulation problems as a preemie. She has severe gastroesophageal reflux and was transitioned off cow's milk per dietician recommendations. Currently on ripple pea protein milk, water, and occasional diluted juice. She has 8-10 wet diapers per 24-hour period and reportedly drinks frequently. She is currently enrolled in feeding therapy, occupational therapy, physical therapy, and will begin speech therapy within the next two weeks. She has also been evaluated by allergy, orthopedic, ophthalmology, and audiology specialists. Her twin sister is reportedly doing well with normal development and similar size. Patient was referred for evaluation by geneticist who noted that Smith-Magenis syndrome can be associated with renal fusion and other kidney abnormalities.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient has significant developmental delay with hypotonia of lower extremities and arms. History of feeding difficulties and apnea with feeding. History of poor temperature regulation as a preemie. Severe gastroesophageal reflux on treatment with GI specialist. No other acute symptoms reported.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Smith-Magenis syndrome (chromosomal deletion). Gastroesophageal reflux disease. History of feeding difficulties and apnea with feeding. Prematurity (34 weeks 3 days gestation). Developmental delay.

MEDICATIONS
Not discussed.

ALLERGIES
Cow's milk intolerance.

FAMILY HISTORY
Older brother (age 9) with autism. Twin sister without known abnormalities.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Family lives in Dallas, Georgia.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Well-nourished female, slightly fussy during examination. Eyes small-appearing. Mild hypotonia of lower extremities and arms. Normal external female genitalia. Heart and lungs examined.

RESULTS
Not discussed.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Katherine is a 22-month-old former 34 and 3-week-old twin with Smith-Magenis syndrome. Several organ systems can be affected by this chromosomal deletion syndrome. Congenital anomalies of the kidney and urinary tract have been reported in the literature. Kidney ultrasound will be obtained today for screening. If abnormalities are found on kidney ultrasound, next steps and future follow-up will be determined. If ultrasound is normal, no further follow-up with nephrology is needed at this time. Family lives in Dallas, Georgia; follow-up should be arranged at town center location if needed.
